syscalls.comment: CAVR addition: runc init after the profile is loaded: checks /proc/thread-self is not overmounted (statx, fstatfs), closes inherited fds (close_range) and starts the container process (execve)
CAVR addition: strace as container root: traces with ptrace, waits with wait4, signals tracees with kill, and `strace -u cavr` drops to UID/GID 10001 (setgroups, setregid, setreuid)

CAVR addition: strace's own start-up: its self-test test_ptrace_seize forks a child that calls pause() and expects it to be killed; without pause the child exits first about 1 run in 40 and strace aborts

CAVR addition: processes the harness and packages start (pip, the import child, threads, os.system, fork); allowed so that each attempt is in the trace, not hidden by EPERM (clone and clone3: see their own entries)

CAVR addition: clone only without CLONE_UNTRACED and without namespace flags (mask 0x7E820000 = Docker's namespace mask 0x7E020000 + CLONE_UNTRACED 0x00800000): an untraced child would run outside strace, and a new user or network namespace opens kernel attack surface; such a clone fails with EPERM, recorded
CAVR addition: clone3 answers ENOSYS (as in Docker's default profile): its flags are in memory, which seccomp cannot inspect; glibc then falls back to clone, which is filtered above
CAVR addition: sockets: allowed so that connect / sendto attempts reach the kernel and are recorded; --network none makes them fail (ENETUNREACH)
CAVR addition: Python start-up, pip install --target and import (measured with strace -c under Docker's default profile, 2026-11-23)
CAVR addition: chdir and fchdir (PR 7): packages that change directory are traced instead of failing with EPERM; the normaliser follows each process's current directory to resolve relative paths
